document.title: Manipulation Transforms: Rotate Object(s) and Size Object(s)
document.purpose: Record the first working rotate and size handle transformations for Data Garden.

summary: Rotate and size handles perform direct transforms through CIRA organisms. The rotate handle rotates the selected object around its center or rotates multiple selected objects around the selected group bounds center. Size handles uniformly scale the selected object or selected group from the same center-based pivot. Preview frames use immediates and the world is mutated only on release.

notes: Both organisms start only from left-button press on the matching handle target in DERIVED.
The previous node-press rotate organism was removed so rotation is handle-driven.
Organisms compute preview/final update maps but do not mutate world state and do not build undo deltas.
Rotation previews update x, y, and angle.
Size previews update x, y, w, and h.
Projection already merges NODE_PREVIEW_MAP fields into projected nodes.

policy: The effect handler captures before fields from the World Model.
The effect handler applies final update maps.
The effect handler records one world revision with undo and redo update_node notes.
No canvas item ids or full-world snapshots are stored in deltas.

behavior: A completed rotate operation is one undoable operation.
A completed size operation is one undoable operation.
Undo restores the prior world_revision_guid through the history checkpoint.
Redo reapplies the committed world revision.
Selection ids and primary selection are preserved when the nodes still exist.
undo-redo.history-shape: History snapshots continue to store workspace state plus world_revision_guid, not full world snapshots.

scaling-policy.multi-selection-pivot: center of selected axis-aligned world bounds
scaling-policy.scale: current pointer distance from pivot divided by starting pointer distance from pivot

known-limitations: Size handles all use center-based uniform scaling regardless of which corner is dragged.
There is no snapping or angle constraint behavior.
Group rotation uses axis-aligned selected world bounds as the pivot source, not oriented bounds.
Handle styling and cursor feedback remain simple.
suggested-next-work: projection reconciliation if visuals become complex
better handle styling and cursor changes
